name: Ausonius Burdigalensis
evidence: Complete 2-volume Loeb Classical Library edition by Hugh G. Evelyn-White includes comprehensive translation of all major works: Ephemeris, Parentalia, Professores, Epitaphs, Eclogues, The Moselle, Order of Famous Cities, and miscellaneous minor works and riddles. Archive.org confirms this represents 'fairly complete translation of Ausonius's extant works' with editors acknowledging corpus evolved through multiple publication phases.

name: Auctor incertus (Cyprianus Carthaginensis?)
evidence: Cyprian's works comprehensively translated in Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 5, with 13 treatises and 82 letters all translated by Robert Ernest Wallis (1886). Includes De Ecclesiae Catholicae Unitate, Ad Donatum, Testimonia ad Quirinum, De Lapsed, and related works. Described as 'well-translated in ANF/NPNF' with public domain access at multiple sites including Christian Classics Ethereal Library.

name: Rodulfus Glaber
evidence: Five Books of the Histories fully translated by John France (Oxford Medieval Texts, ISBN 9780198222415) with critical text and full historical commentary—described as 'first complete English translation since 1866.' The Vita Domni Willelmi Abbatis (Life of St. William) also edited and translated by John France. Both major works accessible with scholarly apparatus.
untranslatedRemainder: None identified beyond these two major works

name: Gaufredus Malaterra
evidence: De Rebus Gestis Rogerii Calabriae et Siciliae (History of the Normans on the First Crusade) fully translated by Kenneth Baxter Wolf, published University of Michigan Press 2005. Complete English translation with scholarly apparatus covering Norman conquest of Sicily. Also accessible via AncientTexts.ai with both Latin text and English translation.

name: Galbertus Brugensis
evidence: De multro, traditione et occisione gloriosi Karoli comitis Flandriarum fully translated in two modern English editions: James Bruce Ross translation (Columbia University Press 1960, 1967) and Jeff Rider translation (Yale University Press 2013). Rider's version based on critical apparatus of all manuscript variants (Corpus Christianorum Medieval Latin Series 1994). Single major surviving work comprehensively accessible.

name: Guigo II prior Carthusiae
evidence: Both major works comprehensively translated: Scala Claustralium (Ladder of Monks) translated by Edmund Colledge & James Walsh (Cistercian Publications 1981); also modern translations by Pascale-Dominique Nau (2013) and online editions. Twelve Meditations included in Colledge & Walsh 1981 edition. Meditation on the Magnificat has uncertain attribution and was excluded by Colledge & Walsh as not meeting their standards. Core authentic works fully available in multiple English versions.
untranslatedRemainder: Meditation on the Magnificat (uncertain attribution, possibly not by Guigo II)

name: Martinus I
evidence: Acts of the Lateran Synod of 649 comprehensively translated by Richard Price, Phil Booth, Catherine Cubitt (Liverpool University Press 2016, Translated Texts for Historians series)—first translation into any modern language. However, searches did not confirm that ALL synodal acts and ALL correspondence attributed to Martin I have been translated. Only the major Lateran Synod of 649 clearly documented as translated into English. Other acts and letters may remain untranslated or only partially translated.
untranslatedRemainder: Possible untranslated synodal acts and correspondence beyond the Lateran Synod of 649; full corpus translation not confirmed

name: Radulfus Cadomensis
evidence: Gesta Tancredi in expeditione Hierosolymitana (The Deeds of Tancred in the Crusade) fully translated by Bernard S. Bachrach and David S. Bachrach (Crusade Texts in Translation 12, Ashgate 2005). First complete English translation of this important First Crusade narrative covering 1096-1105. Available in multiple editions (hardcover, paperback, e-book) through academic publishers and major booksellers.

name: Grimlaicus presbyter
evidence: Regula Solitariorum (Rule for Solitaries) presented for first time in English by Andrew Thornton (Cistercian Publications 2011, Cistercian Studies Series 200). This was the first known rule written for hermits in Latin West. Full translation with notes, appendices, and introduction. Work appears in PL vol. 103, columns 575-664. No other known works by Grimlaicus identified.

name: Avitus Viennensis
evidence: Major works partially translated: (1) Letters: Complete English translation by Danuta Shanzer & Ian Wood (Liverpool University Press 2002, Translated Texts for Historians 38); (2) Poetic works: Biblical and Pastoral Poetry (De spiritualis historiae gestis, 5 books) edited and translated by Michael Roberts (Dumbarton Oaks Medieval Library 2022), plus older Consolatory Praise of Chastity. However, homilies survive only in fragmentary form and full translation status of fragments unclear. Not all sermon material comprehensively translated.
untranslatedRemainder: Homilies survive only in fragmentary form; status of complete translation for all fragments uncertain

name: Optatus Milevitanus
evidence: All seven books of Contra Parmenianum Donatistam fully translated in two English editions: (1) O. R. Vassall-Phillips (1917, Longmans Green & Co.)—classic translation available online and in multiple formats at Internet Archive, CCEL, Tertullian.org; (2) Mark Edwards modern translation (Liverpool University Press, Translated Texts for Historians series)—first new translation since 1917 with contemporary scholarship and annotation. Comprehensive coverage of his anti-Donatist polemic.

name: Columbanus Hibernus
evidence: Major works comprehensively available: (1) Letters of Columbanus—complete English translations accessible via CELT (Corpus of Electronic Texts, University College Cork); (2) Sermons of Columbanus—full English translations via CELT; (3) Penitentials and Rules: The Penitential of Columbanus and monastic rules (Regula Monachorum, Regula Coenobialis) translated with parallel Latin-English texts by G.S.M. Walker and Ludwig Bieler. Works in PL vol. 80. Comprehensive Irish monastic corpus accessible in English.
